ladder.name: Dam break vs Martin & Moyce (1952)

config.domain: 15a wide x 2a tall x thin single-cell slab (2D, empty front/back)

nondimensionalisation.source: arXiv:2108.08769 (Xie 2021), Sec 3.3.2 / Fig 7, verified against page image not just text extraction

reference_data.source: Martin & Moyce (1952), original tabulated data not located; digitised from Fig. 7 of arXiv:2108.08769 (Xie 2021) which plots the 1952 experimental points
reference_data.digitisation_method: programmatic pixel-position detection (axis-tick pixel clusters for calibration, cross-marker centroid detection), not manual eyeballing

feasibility_evidence.solver_completion: reached endTime=0.8s (T~10.5) on all 3 runs, no divergence, no FPE
feasibility_evidence.alpha_boundedness: within MULES numerical tolerance (~1e-6), no unbounded blow-up

gate_result.primary_metric: surge front position Z vs nondimensional time T

comparison.note: confounded by proximity to domain far wall (15a)

coarse_mesh_same_metric.note: sign flipped vs medium mesh -- refinement did NOT converge toward reference, ruling out simple under-resolution as sole cause

bc_control_test.hypothesis: open-top atmosphere BC lets air vent too easily, over-speeding the front vs the reference paper's fully closed box
bc_control_test.result: REFUTED -- closed-box rerun gave essentially identical front trajectory to open-top run

comparison.note: near edge of digitised reference range

secondary_check.interpretation: bulk column depletion tracks the reference much more closely than the leading-edge front position

cause: Not a boundary-condition artifact (ruled out by closed-box vs open-top A/B test)
Not simple under-resolution (mesh refinement flipped the sign of the error rather than converging)
Correlated with near-wall sampling height used to define front position from the discretised VOF field; the leading edge is thin and not vertical at these resolutions
Bulk quantity (column height decay), less sensitive to this effect, agrees with reference to within ~10%
lesson: A single alpha=0.5 crossing at the first cell above the floor is not a mesh-independent front-position definition for VOF dam-break validation; needs either a genuine multi-mesh Richardson study or an isosurface-based front extraction
Programmatic pixel-position digitisation (axis-tick calibration + marker centroid detection) of a published figure is more reliable than eyeballing and should be the default method going forward
Gate failed as measured; shipped as a documented failure per campaign hard rules
